jobs.occupation: Software Engineer (f/m/d) - Life Science and Diagnostics (Informatiker/in)
jobs.description:
Overview  

 
At QIAGEN, we are driven by a simple but powerful vision: making improvements in life possible.  

We’re dedicated to revolutionizing science and healthcare for the better. From our entrepreneurial roots to our current global presence, we've grown into a force for positive change. With thousands of employees across six continents, collaboration is our greatest strength. We’re always striving to identify talented individuals to join our exceptional teams. 
 
We have played a pivotal role in shaping modern science and healthcare, and we're just getting started. If you're someone who thrives on new challenges, values diversity and wants to make a tangible difference in people's lives, then QIAGEN is the place for you. 

 

At QIAGEN, every day is an opportunity to make a real-life impact. 

 

Join us, grow with us, and together, let's shape the future of biological discovery. 

‎

About this opportunity

In the position of a (Junior) Software Engineer (f/m/d) in Life Science and Diagnostics at QIAGEN, you will be making improvements in life possible – every working day. We are looking for you to help us shape our product development with skill and passion. You will work with our system and software teams to develop instrument control software for laboratory devices as well as data analysis software to process test results helping our customers to get valuable insights from a biological sample.

Your Tasks
* As a Software Engineer you will typically work in project teams of 5-10 people and gain experience in different roles throughout the life cycle of a software development project.
* You will start as a software developer or (automated) software tester in one of our scrum teams. Throught your professional career you will have the opportunity to grow into senior roles such as senior engineer, product owner, software architect or verification manager.  
* You will work across teams and across sites to generate the best possible solution for our products in a complex environment of Biology, Chemistry, Mechanics, Electronics and Software.
* You will be based at QIAGEN Hilden, our operational headquarter and will have the opportunity to visit our international development sites in Aarhus, Denmark or Wroclaw, Poland to strengthen and refine your software development capabilities.

Your Profile
* You have a master’s degree in computer science, with a minor in medicine, science or engineering
* You show a strong interest in software and product development and have already gained first professional experience.
* You love science and have a strong analytical mindset that strives to analyze, understand and solve problems.
* You are highly organized, work independently and easily adapt to changing work environment.
* You show excellent communication skills in both, English and German (C1 level)
* Ideally, you are familiar with working with AI-powered development tools or large language models to automate software development lifecycle processes. Experience with connecting AI agents with third-party systems using Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a plus

Please provide a transcript of record and an employer's reference if applicable.

What we offer  

 

* Bonus/Commission  

* Local benefits   

* Referral Program  

* Volunteer Day  

* Internal Academy (QIALearn)   

* Employee Assistance Program   

* Hybrid work (conditional to your role) 

 

Our people are the heartbeat of everything we do. Passion drives us as we push boundaries to innovate and evolve. We inspire with our leadership and make an impact with our actions. We cultivate a collaborative, supportive environment where each individual and team can flourish. We champion accountability and encourage entrepreneurial thinking.   

 

QIAGEN is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a veteran, or disability.

The University Hospital Bonn (UKB) is one of Germany’s leading university hospitals, combining top-level performance in medicine and research withexcellence in teaching. Each year, more than half a million patients receive inpatient and outpatient care at the UKB. Around 3,500 students study medicine and dentistry here, and over 600 people are trained annually in healthcare professions. With approximately 9,900 employees, the UKB is the third-largest employer in the Bonn/Rhein-Sieg region. In the Focus hospital ranking, the UKB ranksfirst among universityhospitalsin North Rhine-Westphalia andsecond nationwide in terms of case mix index (case severity). In 2024, the UKB raised nearly €100 million in third-party funding for research, development, and teaching. The F.A.Z. Institute has named the UKB “Germany’s Training Champion” and “Germany’s Most Attractive Employer” for the fourth consecutive year.

The arbovirus research group of PD Dr. Beate Kümmerer at the Institute of Virology at the University Hospital Bonn (Germany) is looking for a highly motivated

PhD student (m/f/d)

to join our team and explore the fascinating biology of orthoflavivirus-host interaction in mosquitoes and vertebrates. The PhD position (65% E13 salary according to DFG recommendations), initially limited to three years, is advertisedwithin the framework of the DFG-funded CRC/Transregio 237 “Nucleic Acid Immunity” and is to be filled by January 2027.

The position is offered on a fixed-term basis until December 31, 2029.
Mosquito-borne RNA viruses, such as dengue, yellow fever, and Zika virus, cause severe disease outbreaks worldwide. As climate change drives the spread of mosquito vectors, the regions affected by these viruses continue to expand. Orthoflaviviruses have evolved multiple strategies to evade innate immune recognition, thereby promoting viral replication and pathogenesis. The project aims to elucidate how viral RNA structures and RNA modifications shape innate immune recognition. A particular focus will be the identification of mosquito proteins that recognize viral cap0 RNA and the characterization of viral immune antagonists in both mosquito and vertebrate hosts. We hope to gain mechanistic insights into virus-host interactions that support the development of innovative antiviral therapies and sustainable vector control strategies.

Methods: Molecular biology methods, cell culture and virological methods, RNA-protein and protein-protein interaction studies, gene expression analyses, cellular knock-down, as well as research involving mosquitoes.

Master’s degree in life sciences
Enthusiasm for research in a collaborative environment
Commitment to the research project
Profound knowledge in basic molecular biological methods and cell culture
Experience in virology and/or protein-RNA/protein interaction studies would be ideal
Eligibility, willingness and physical fitness to work in a biosafety lev el (BSL) 3 laboratory
Interest in working with live mosquitoes
Motivation to learn new methods
Fluent oral and written English

A 3-year PhD position (65% TV-L E13) with strong mentoring and integration into a high-profile research network (CRC/Transregio 237)
An interdisciplinary research environment at one of Germany’s top universities
A highly collaborative research team

Access to further education in university and non-university courses
Integration into the Bonn International Graduate School (BIGS) Immunosciences and Infection

Responsible and diverse: A position with plenty of room for creativity and responsibility within a supportive and collegial team

Fair compensation: Pay according to the TV-L collective agreement, including annual bonus and company pension scheme

Family-friendly flexibility: Flexible working time models, access to a place in our company daycare center, and programs supporting employees returning from parental leave

Smart commuting: Excellent connection to the SWB public transport network

jobs.description:
A Snapshot of Your Day 

A Snapshot of Your Day
Join our global and diverse Gas Services (GS) organization, where putting the customer at the heart of every decision and continuously improving how we operate are the foundation of quality. Quality is more than reporting, firefighting, and correcting issues after the fact — it is about turning experience into sustainable learning and lasting improvement.
As Service Quality Professional you will act as a trusted partner and point of contact for our Regional Service Unit (RSU), driving important Service Quality initiatives and process improvements across GS. You will connect the Regional Service Units, Global Service Operations, and other stakeholders on key quality topics — sharing best practices, driving common standards, and creating transparency. Balancing global, strategic initiatives with selective, hands-on regional support, you will help ensure quality programs are successfully implemented and that sustainable improvements — measured by non-conformance costs (NCC) and customer satisfaction (NPS) — are achieved.

How You’ll Make an Impact 

* Act as a reliable, competent point of contact for RSU on quality topics, hurdles, and questions, ensuring RSU interests are considered in EQS decision-making.
* Enable the RSU QM community by providing the support needed to successfully implement quality programs and achieve measurable, sustainable improvements in Service Quality.
* Drive global focus-area initiatives — Customer Excellence / NPS, Service CAPA, and Process Management — in alignment with RSU needs, EQS stakeholders, and process owners.
* Support and govern prioritized improvement projects across regions, and global functions, ensuring visible, customer-felt impact.
* Foster process implementation, harmonization, and comparability of results across RSUs to reduce complexity and boost efficiency.
* Act proactively based on data — leverage dashboards, KPIs, and AI-supported insights to identify focus areas and accelerate decisions.
* Identify global, systemic issues and initiate targeted, cross-regional improvement actions, applying structured problem-solving and continuous-improvement methods.
* Facilitate best-practice sharing by highlighting regional successes and systematically addressing areas for improvement across the GS Service network.
* Provide transparency through structured reporting, and maintenance of relevant frameworks (e.g., Hoshin Kanri, Quality DoR)

What You Bring

* University degree in engineering, business, quality management, or a comparable field.
* Solid experience in quality management, process management, service operations, or continuous improvement, ideally within a complex, international, service-oriented organization.
* Understanding of quality methods and standards (e.g., ISO 9001), including non-conformance management, and their integration into daily processes.
* Experience applying continuous improvement and problem-solving methodologies (e.g., Lean Six Sigma, root-cause analysis) across multiple organizations.
* Affinity for digitalization and AI to make quality and process knowledge more accessible and processes smarter (e.g., SEPH, BIC Cloud, and related tools).
* Excellent stakeholder management, great communicator, and organizational skills, with the ability to build trust across cultures, regions, and hierarchy levels.
* Proactive, self-driven, and customer-centric mindset, balancing global strategic goals with pragmatic regional support.
* Fluency in English; further languages are a plus given the global scope of the role.

About the Team

Our Gas Services division offers Low-emission power generation through service and decarbonization. Zero or low emission power generation and all gas turbines under one roof, steam turbines and generators. Decarbonization opportunities through service offerings, modernization, and digitalization of the fleet.

Who is Siemens Energy? 

At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.

Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.      

Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideo

Our Commitment to Diversity 

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences. 

Rewards/Benefits 

* In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme
* We also offer the opportunity to become a Siemens Energy shareholder
* We offer our employees the opportunity to work flexibly and remotely, and our inspiring offices provide space for collaboration and creativity
* The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. We provide them with the opportunities to learn and develop in a self-determined way, various attractive programmes and learning materials are available for this purpose
* In relation to the "compatibility of family and work", we have a wide range of offers, e.g. flexible working time models, childcare places at many locations, the possibility of trial part-time work or even a sabbatical 

We value equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities.

Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU) is one of the largest universities in Germany. Thanks to its location in the Rhine-Main science region, the university can unfold to its full potential and showcase its innovative power and dynamism. Its status as a comprehensive university allows for multidisciplinary learning and teaching and has great potential for internationally renowned, interdisciplinary research. Almost all of its institutes are located on a single campus close to the Mainz city center - creating a lively academic culture for researchers, teaching staff, and students from every continent.
PhD student: Plant RNA Biology
The Wachter group at the Institute for Molecular Physiology (Faculty 10: Biology of Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz) investigates the molecular mechanisms and biological functions of alternative RNA splicing in plants. Our recent work identified a structured mRNA element that regulates specific DEAD-box helicase genes and revealed their critical role in controlling alternative splicing. Intriguingly, these functions appear to be linked to unique C-terminal features of the respective helicases. As a member of an interdisciplinary and international research team, you will investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying the splicing-regulatory activity of these DEAD-box helicases, with a particular focus on the functional relevance of RGG motifs, subcellular localisation, and their potential involvement in phase separation. In collaboration with the Weinberg group (University Halle-Wittenberg), you will also explore how helicase targeting of pre-mRNA structural elements may intersect with the binding of splicing regulators to determine splice site choice. Your research will employ a multidisciplinary approach that integrates molecular biology, RNA biochemistry, cell biology, and plant physiology, with Arabidopsis thaliana as the primary model system. You will benefit from extensive expertise, various core facilities, and a completely new research infrastructure. The PhD project is funded by the DFG and can be integrated in the international PhD programme (IPP) in Mainz.
Applying state-of-the-art techniques for gene-specific and genome-wide analyses of RNA biology, including transcriptome-wide profiling of alternative splicing and mapping of protein-RNA interactions
Employing in vitro and in vivo experimental systems to address different levels of complexity and advance our understanding of the biological functions
Contributing to teaching activities for Bachelor’s and Master’s students within our group
Assisting with organizational and administrative tasks
Presenting your research findings in oral and written form, including conference contributions, reports, and manuscripts

Thinking of doing your PhD in the Life Sciences? The International PhD Programme (IPP) Mainz is offering talented scientists the chance to work on cutting edge research projects. As an IPP PhD student, you will join a community of exceptional scientists working on diverse topics ranging from how organisms age or how our DNA is repaired, to how epigenetics regulates cellular identity or neural memory. The research group of Johannes Mayer offers the following PhD project:
Circulating myeloid cells, which include monocytes, dendritic cells and granulocytes, are short lived and continuously replenished by the bone marrow. Under non-inflammatory conditions, myelopoiesis follows relatively ordered differentiation routes that sustain circulating monocytes and granulocytes and seed tissue macrophage and dendritic cell compartments. Both mature cells and bone marrow progenitors have the capacity to rapidly reconfigure during local and systemic inflammation, with cell-cell communication cues from stromal, endothelial, and lymphoid niches helping to calibrate output and function.

Myeloid cell activation and exhaustion has both been described on a mature cell and progenitor cell level, leading to emergency myelopoiesis or hematopoietic halt/shock. Using single-cell and multi-omic profiling integrated with trajectory inference and ligand-receptor/network modeling, this project will establish a perturbation landscape of different myeloid cells and their progenitors in the context of different inflammatory cues using in silico modelling and in vitro validation.

PhD project: Defining Myeloid cell Ageing and its immunological impact on a single cell level

In our lab, we have established an integrated toolkit to study myeloid cell biology at single-cell resolution. Combined with datamining, LLM studies, in vitro activation and CRISPR/Cas9 perturbation screen, you will study the activation and exhaustion landscape of different myeloid cell types and their progenitors. In addition, you will work together with the team to characterize inflammatory models in vivo that span both systemic and local inflammation and track myeloid cell and progenitor activation and exhaustion over time.

This PhD requires a strong background in immunology, previous experience with both wet lab and dry lab work on a single-cell level and a willingness to work with in vivo animal models, including handling, experimental design and tissue processing and analysis.

If you are interested in this project, please select Mayer (Activate) as your project preference in the IPP application platform.
